title: LLM Agent Cost and Latency: Quick Revision Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on controlling cost and latency in LLM agents: token accounting, prompt caching, model routing, streaming, parallel tools, retrieval caching, timeouts and fallbacks, and tracing. Ordered from mental model to workflow, usage, mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Cost and Latency Mental Model
points: Cost = input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price; output tokens cost roughly 3-5× input tokens, so cut output length first
Agent loops resend the whole history every turn, so input tokens grow quadratically with the number of steps
Latency = time to first token (TTFT, driven by input size) + output tokens × per-token decode time
Four levers: send fewer tokens, reuse tokens (caching), use a cheaper model (routing), do work concurrently (streaming, parallel calls)
Interview trap: measure cost per successful task, not per request, because retries and failed runs hide in the total

chapters.title: Token Accounting and Prompt Caching
points: Log usage from every response: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, tagged by run_id, step and model
Prompt caching reuses a prefix of the prompt: cache reads cost about 10% of base input price, cache writes cost about 125%, so it pays off from the second hit
Cache matches on an exact prefix, so order the prompt: tools, then system prompt, then stable docs, then conversation, then the new user turn
Cache entries expire after a short TTL (about 5 minutes by default), and each hit refreshes it; low-traffic prompts never get hits
Cache breakers: timestamps or request IDs in the system prompt, reordered tools, edited earlier messages; check cache_read_tokens > 0 to confirm hits

chapters.title: Model Routing and Streaming
points: Model routing sends easy steps (classify, extract, summarize, tool arg formatting) to a small model and hard steps (planning, multi-step reasoning) to a large one
Router types: rule-based (task type, input length), classifier-based (small model scores difficulty), cascade (try small, escalate if confidence or validation fails)
Cascade cost check: escalation rate × large-model cost + small-model cost must stay below always-large cost, or routing loses money
Streaming sends tokens as generated (SSE): total time is unchanged but TTFT drops, so the UI feels fast
Streaming gotchas: tool-call arguments arrive as partial JSON, so buffer until the block ends before parsing; handle mid-stream errors and client disconnects by cancelling the upstream call

chapters.title: Parallel Tools, Retrieval Caching, Timeouts and Fallbacks
points: Parallel tool calls: when the model returns several independent tool_use blocks in one turn, run them concurrently (asyncio.gather) and return all results in a single message; latency becomes the slowest call, not the sum
Never parallelize calls with dependencies or side-effect ordering (write then read); set a concurrency cap to avoid rate limits
Retrieval cache: key on the normalized query plus index version and filters; exact-match is safe, semantic cache (embedding similarity threshold) saves more but risks wrong answers
Invalidate the retrieval cache on index or document updates and set a TTL; never cache user-private results under a shared key
Timeouts at every layer: per-tool, per-model-call and a whole-run deadline; retry only idempotent calls, with exponential backoff plus jitter and a max attempts cap
Fallback chain: retry, then alternate model or provider, then cached or degraded answer, then a clear error; a circuit breaker stops calling a dependency that keeps failing

chapters.title: Tracing Agent Runs
points: A trace is one agent run; spans are its steps (LLM call, tool call, retrieval), nested by parent_id, so a loop reads as a tree
Record per span: input, output, model, token counts, cost, latency, status, and error; propagate one trace_id through every tool and service
Use OpenTelemetry spans, or an LLM tool such as Langfuse or LangSmith, to view the timeline and find the slowest and costliest step
Attach metadata for slicing: user_id, prompt version, route chosen, cache hit or miss, fallback used
Common mistakes: logging raw PII or secrets in prompts, sampling away the failed runs, and tracing only the LLM call while tool latency stays invisible

chapters.title: Cost and Latency Cheat Sheet
points: Cost formula: in_tokens × in_price + out_tokens × out_price; cache read ≈ 0.1×, cache write ≈ 1.25× input price
Cache-friendly prompt order: tools, system, stable context, history, new turn; no timestamps up front; verify cache_read_tokens > 0
Routing: rules first, then small-model cascade with escalation; track escalation rate and quality per route
Streaming lowers TTFT only; parallel independent tool calls cost the slowest call; retrieval cache key = query + filters + index version
Resilience: per-call timeout, whole-run deadline, retry only idempotent calls with backoff and jitter, fallback chain, circuit breaker
Trace every run: trace_id, span per step, tokens, cost, latency, error; alert on cost per task and p95 latency
